phrases.arabic: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ يَجِبُ أَنْ أُغَادِرَ الْفُنْدُق؟
phrases.transliteration: fii ayyi saa3atin yajibu an ughaadira al-funduq?

reply.english: You're welcome, we wish you a pleasant stay.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Hello, I have a reservation.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Welcome, under whose name?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Under the name Nour.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Yes, a room for two people for three nights.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Is breakfast included with the room?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Yes, from seven until nine.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Can I see the room first?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Of course. Here is the key.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.english: Where is the elevator?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: On your right after the door.

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.arabic: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ يَجِبُ أَنْ أُغَادِرَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: fii ayyi saa3atin yajibu an ughaadira?
dialogue.english: What time do I need to check out?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Before twelve noon.

lessons.culture: At a hotel reception in any Arab country, staff speak Fusha or a mix with the local dialect, and a polite مِنْ فَضْلِك goes a long way. Breakfast is often included, and check-out is usually around noon.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ يُوجَدُ مَقْعَدٌ شَاغِرٌ فِي الْحَافِلَةِ الْقَادِمَة؟
phrases.transliteration: hal yoojadu maq3adun shaaghirun fii al-7aafilati al-qaadima?

reply.english: You're welcome, have a good trip.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Hello, I want to book a bus ticket.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Welcome. To where?

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Do you have tickets to Aleppo?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، مُتَوَفِّرَة. هَلْ تُرِيدُ ذَهَابًا وَإِيَابًا؟
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, mutawaffira. hal tureedu dhahaaban wa iyaaban?
dialogue.english: Yes, available. Do you want a round trip?

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: No, I want a one-way ticket only.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: يُوجَدُ مَقْعَدٌ شَاغِرٌ فِي الْحَافِلَةِ الْقَادِمَة.
dialogue.transliteration: yoojadu maq3adun shaaghirun fii al-7aafilati al-qaadima.
dialogue.english: There is a free seat on the next bus.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: What time does it leave?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: At eight in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Can I pay by card?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: Yes, here is your ticket.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Thanks. How long does the trip take?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.english: About five hours. Have a good trip.

pair.english: Do you have tickets to Aleppo?
What time does the bus leave?
How long does the trip take?

lessons.culture: Intercity buses and coaches are the usual way to travel between Arab cities, and tickets are bought at the ticket window or online. Students often get a discount if they show a card, so asking is normal.

reply.english: At the end of the hall.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Where is the check-in counter?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: فِي آخِرِ الْقَاعَة. جَوَازُ السَّفَرِ مِنْ فَضْلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: fii aakhiri al-qaa3a. jawaazu as-safari min fadlik.
dialogue.english: At the end of the hall. Your passport please.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: I have my passport and my ticket.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: How many bags am I allowed to take?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: حَقِيبَتَانِ. هَلْ هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَةُ زَائِدَةُ الْوَزْن؟
dialogue.english: Two bags. Is this bag overweight?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: I don't think so. Where is the boarding gate?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: الْبَوَّابَةُ الثَّالِثَة. تُقْلِعُ الطَّائِرَةُ فِي الْعَاشِرَة.
dialogue.transliteration: al-bawwaabatu ath-thaalitha. tuqli3u at-taa2iratu fii al-3aashira.
dialogue.english: Gate three. The plane departs at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.arabic: جَوَازُ السَّفَرِ مِنْ فَضْلِك. هَلْ أَتَيْتَ لِلسِّيَاحَةِ أَمْ لِلْعَمَل؟
dialogue.transliteration: jawaazu as-safari min fadlik. hal ataita lis-siyaa7ati am lil-3amal?
dialogue.english: Your passport please. Are you coming for tourism or work?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: For tourism.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.english: How long will you stay here?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Two weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.english: Do you have anything to declare?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: No, I don't have anything.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.english: Welcome.

lessons.culture: At the airport the border officer usually asks short questions in Fusha or the local dialect: purpose of the visit, length of stay, anything to declare. A calm, polite answer and a greeting like أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا from the officer mark a smooth arrival.

phrases.arabic: عَوَّضَ اللهُ عَلَيْكَ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ تُحَلُّ الْمُشْكِلَة
phrases.transliteration: 3awwada allaahu 3alayka, in shaa2a allaahu tu7allu al-mushkila

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Excuse me, I lost my bag.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.english: Certainly, what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.arabic: لَمْ أَجِدْهَا بَعْدَ الرِّحْلَة، وَتَكَسَّرَتْ حَقِيبَتِي الْأُخْرَى.
dialogue.transliteration: lam ajidhaa ba3da ar-ri7la, wa takassarat 7aqeebatee al-ukhraa.
dialogue.english: I couldn't find it after the flight, and my other bag got broken.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: أَيْنَ مَكْتَبُ الشَّكَاوَى؟ هُوَ عَلَى يَسَارِكَ.
dialogue.english: The complaints office? It is on your left.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Thanks. The plane is also very delayed.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.english: I apologise. Do you have another booking?

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.arabic: هُنَاكَ مُشْكِلَةٌ فِي الْحَجْز. فَاتَتْنِي الرِّحْلَة، مَاذَا أَفْعَل؟
dialogue.transliteration: hunaaka mushkilatun fii al-7ajz. faatatnee ar-ri7la, maadha af3al?
dialogue.english: There's a problem with the booking. I missed the flight, what do I do?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَغْيِيرِ الرِّحْلَة. تَعَالَ مَعِي.
dialogue.transliteration: ta7taaju ilaa taghyeeri ar-ri7la. ta3aala ma3ee.
dialogue.english: You need to change the flight. Come with me.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Nobody answered me a moment ago.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.english: I apologise again. We will help you now.

dialogue.speaker: Traveller
dialogue.english: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.arabic: عَوَّضَ اللهُ عَلَيْكَ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ تُحَلُّ الْمُشْكِلَة.
dialogue.transliteration: 3awwada allaahu 3alayka, in shaa2a allaahu tu7allu al-mushkila.
dialogue.english: May God make up for it, God willing the problem will be solved.

pair.english: I missed the flight, what do I do?

response.english: You need to change the flight.

lessons.culture: When something goes wrong while travelling, people ask for help politely with مِنْ فَضْلِك and explain the problem in a short sentence. A common thing to say to someone facing a setback is عَوَّضَ اللهُ عَلَيْكَ, and the usual answer is آمِين.

challenge.title: A trip from start to finish
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you book a ticket, check in at a hotel, ask about breakfast and check-out, and report a lost bag politely.
required_elements: a request for a ticket with the price asked
a hotel reservation under a name
a question about breakfast or check-out time
a problem explained with فَقَدْتُ or فَاتَتْنِي
a polite request with مِنْ فَضْلِك and thanks

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: مِنْ فَضْلِك، أُرِيدُ تَذْكِرَةَ ذَهَابٍ وَإِيَابٍ إِلَى حَلَب.
dialogue.transliteration: min fadlik, ureedu tadhkirata dhahaabin wa iyaabin ilaa 7alab.
dialogue.english: Please, I want a round-trip ticket to Aleppo.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّلْ. كَمْ سِعْرُ التَّذْكِرَة؟ مِئَةُ دُولَار.
dialogue.transliteration: tafaddal. kam si3ru at-tadhkira? mi2atu doolaar.
dialogue.english: Here you are. The ticket price? One hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا. عِنْدِي حَجْزٌ فِي الْفُنْدُقِ بِاسْمِ يُوسُف.
dialogue.english: Thanks. I have a hotel booking under the name Yusuf.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.english: Welcome. Here is the key.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Is breakfast included with the room?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، وَيَجِبُ أَنْ تُغَادِرَ قَبْلَ الظُّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, wa yajibu an tughaadira qabla az-zuhr.
dialogue.english: Yes, and you need to check out before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: فَقَدْتُ حَقِيبَتِي فِي الْمَطَار. أَيْنَ مَكْتَبُ الشَّكَاوَى؟
dialogue.transliteration: faqadtu 7aqeebatee fii al-mataar. ayna maktabu ash-shakaawaa?
dialogue.english: I lost my bag at the airport. Where is the complaints office?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.english: We will help you. May God make up for it.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Amen. Thank you very much.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.english: You're welcome. A pleasant stay.
